suṣumnā
------------------------------------------
Suṣumnā is the central nāḍī or canal passing through the centre of the spinal cord. It is called by several other names such as śūnya, padavī, ब्रह्मरन्ध्र, mahāpatha, śāmbhavī and so on.
The other two nāḍīs—the iḍā and the piṅgalā—entwine it.
When प्राण (life-force) is made to flow through this by proper exercises like कुम्भक, the मिन्द् becomes absolutely steady. This steadiness is called मनोन्मनी condition.
The कुण्डलिनी, when awakened, rises through this सुषुम्ना and reaches the sahasrāracakra after piercing through all the other चक्रस्.
See also CAKRAS.

Suśrutasaṁhitā
------------------------------------------
Hindu sages paid as much attention to the life here and now as to the one hereafter. That is why many great sages developed secular sciences too, in the various fields of mundane life.
Since our body is the most wonderful gift of God, and since we can achieve whatever we want in life only through it, to keep it in a fit condition is the primary duty of every human being.
The science of आयुर्वेद (‘Science of Health and Longevity’) aims exactly at this.
Out of the several standard treatises on this subject, the Carakasaṁhitā of चरक and the Suśrutasaṁhitā of सुश्रुत have carved for themselves a unique place in the field of health science in ancient India.
Whereas the former is a work on medicine, the latter is predominantly on surgery.
Tradition considers सुश्रुत as one of the sons of the sage विश्वामित्र and a disciple of दिवोदास (the king of काशी, and reincarnation of धन्वन्तरि, the physician of gods). He might have lived anywhere between 1000 B. C. and 600 B. C.
The work is in the form of sūtras, anuṣṭubh ślokas as also prose.
Two commentaries are available on this treatise:
Bhānumatī by Cakrapāṇi (A.

); Nibandhasaṅgraha by Ḍalhaṇa (12th century A. D.)
The Book, as available now, is in six sthānas or sections. Each sthāna is divided into adhyāyas or chapters containing ślokas (verses, sūtras and passages).
The following table gives an idea of the work:
Section Adhyāyas Ślokas
1. Sūtrasthāna 46 1409
2. Nidānasthāna 16 520
3. Śārīrasthāna 10 440
4. Cikitsāsthāna 40 1886
5. Kalpasthāna 8 560
6. Uttaratantra 66 2317
Total 186 7132

The contents may be summarised briefly:
1. Sūtrasthāna (Introduction)
Origin of आयुर्वेद; instruments and implements to be got ready before surgery; operation procedures and post-operative care; uses of machines and surgical instruments; ointments and medicinal drinks; cauterisation; taking out bad blood using leeches; bandaging.
2. Nidānasthāna (Diagnosis)
Sixteen serious diseases like imbalance of vāta or wind, fistula, leprosy, diabetes and so on; their causes and cure.
3. Śārīrasthāna (Physiology and Anatomy)
Embryology; sensitive places in the body; blood-vessels and nervous system; child-birth and other allied topics.
4. Cikitsāsthāna (Diagnosis and Treatment)
Diseases like fistula, leprosy, fractures, kindney-stones etc., and the methods of their operation are dealt with here.
This section has many more details than are found in other similar works like the Carakasaṁhitā or the Astāṅgahṛdaya.
5. Kalpasthāna (Toxicology)
How to remedy the poisons that might have been consumed through ड़ोओद् materials and offsetting the evil effects of the poisons by snake bite or bites by insects and so on, are the subject matter of this section.
6. Uttaratantra (Supplement)
Also called Uttarasthāna, this last section is fairly voluminous. It contains the descriptions and remedies of several diseases like those of the eyes, the ears, the nose, the head and the mouth.
This book is perhaps a later addition.
It is remarkable that this work prescribes in the very beginning (

-10) the necessary qualifications of a disciple to become a good vaidya (doctor/surgeon) as also the obligations of the teacher.
Suśruta permits even a śūdra of good physique and conduct to be trained in this science.
See also AṢṬĀṄGAHṚDAYA, ĀYURVEDA and CARAKASAṀHITĀ.
